name: Residual resistivity ratio (RRR) of SRF-grade niobium by four-point resistance at room temperature and ~10 K
plain_name: Measure how pure a niobium sheet is by comparing its electrical resistance warm and just above 9 K
description: Quality control of niobium sheet and welds for SRF cavities: strip samples are clamped in a four-point fixture, cooled in a liquid-helium dewar and slowly warmed; resistance just above the ~9.3 K superconducting transition (~10 K) is divided into the room-temperature resistance to give RRR.
keywords: Measure how pure a niobium sheet is by comparing its electrical resistance warm and just above 9 K

sources.citation: Recent RRR Measurements on Niobium for Superconducting RF Cavities at Fermilab (Bauer et al., SRF2005, TUP47)
A Multi-Sample Residual Resistivity Ratio System for High Quality Superconductor Measurements (Spradlin, Valente-Feliciano, Reece, SRF2015, TUPB063)

reported_equipment: Fermilab Technical Division temperature sensor calibration facility
JLab multi-sample RRR system (liquid helium dewar, JLab vertical test area)

requirements.rationale: RRR uses resistivity at 300 K and at 10 K in the same fixture.
Four-point probe leads and thermometer wiring must reach the samples.
Fermilab samples are ~75 mm long strips (~2x2 mm2).
The series-connected samples are driven with 100 mA.
Both reported systems cool the samples with liquid helium.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
